fault: brake pad off-centre, rubbing the rim
safety_notes: Test the brakes before you ride.

steps.instruction: Loosen the brake pad bolt a half turn with a hex key. Do not remove it.
steps.expected_visual_state: A hex key sits in the pad bolt and the pad can slide slightly.
common_mistakes: Using the wrong size key and rounding the bolt
steps.illustration_prompt: Blueprint-style line drawing: Loosen the brake pad bolt a half turn with a hex key. Do not remove it. No text.

steps.instruction: Slide the pad so it sits flat on the metal braking surface, clear of the tyre.
steps.expected_visual_state: The whole pad face lines up with the braking surface of the rim.
common_mistakes: Pad too low on the rim
steps.illustration_prompt: Blueprint-style line drawing: Slide the pad so it sits flat on the metal braking surface, clear of the tyre. No text.

steps.instruction: Squeeze the brake lever and hold it, then tighten the pad bolt.
steps.expected_visual_state: The lever is held in and the bolt is snug with the pad still flat.
common_mistakes: Letting the pad twist while tightening
steps.illustration_prompt: Blueprint-style line drawing: Squeeze the brake lever and hold it, then tighten the pad bolt. No text.

steps.instruction: Spin the wheel and check the gap is even on both sides of the rim.
steps.expected_visual_state: The wheel spins freely with no rubbing sound.
common_mistakes: Ignoring a wobbling wheel that needs truing
steps.illustration_prompt: Blueprint-style line drawing: Spin the wheel and check the gap is even on both sides of the rim. No text.

steps.instruction: Squeeze the lever hard and push the bike forward to test the brake.
steps.expected_visual_state: The brake grips firmly and releases cleanly.
steps.illustration_prompt: Blueprint-style line drawing: Squeeze the lever hard and push the bike forward to test the brake. No text.
